_how_to_use: This file is in the SAME schema as the SOP Builder JSON, plus '_perm' tags and a '_personas' assembly map. To generate a persona SOP: (1) pick the persona in _personas; (2) keep only steps/checklist/issues whose id is listed for that persona; (3) replace cover fields and any [bracketed] placeholders with client values or leave blank to render as placeholders; (4) delete the _library/_personas/_perm keys or leave them — the builder renderer ignores unknown keys; (5) paste into the builder and download. Never invent client names, dates, SLAs or IDs.

P1_read_only_responder.label: Read Only · Responder / Distribution member
P1_read_only_responder.phases_note: Use phases as-is; this persona only acts in 'Respond'.
P1_read_only_responder.cannot_do: Cannot create RFIs, cannot assign or close them, cannot see private RFIs unless on the distribution list.

access.levelMeaning: You can view RFIs you are named on, receive notifications, and respond when you are the assignee. You cannot create, assign or close RFIs.
notIncluded: Create RFIs — handled by Standard users.
Assign, respond-and-close or manage RFIs — handled by the RFI Manager.
Private RFIs unless you are on the distribution list.

P2_standard_creator.label: Standard · RFI Creator (e.g. Site Engineer / Foreman)
P2_standard_creator.cannot_do: Creates RFIs in Draft only — cannot assign the official RFI number, cannot send the RFI to the design team, cannot respond-and-close. The RFI Manager does this. Visibility of others' RFIs depends on project settings.

access.levelMeaning: You can create RFIs in Draft with your question, drawings and photos, and submit them to the RFI Manager. You can respond when assigned and track your own items.
notIncluded: Assign the official RFI number or send the RFI to the design team — RFI Manager.
Respond-and-close or reopen RFIs — RFI Manager / Admin.
Tool settings and the permissions table — RFIs Admin.

P3_rfi_manager.label: Standard + 'Act as RFI Manager' granular permission
P3_rfi_manager.cannot_do: Manager actions apply only to RFIs they created or where they are the designated RFI Manager. Cannot edit or delete other users' RFIs, cannot change tool settings or the permissions table.

access.levelMeaning: You manage the full lifecycle of RFIs you create or are designated RFI Manager for — opening, numbering, distributing, chasing, marking the official response and closing.

granular.name: Act as RFI Manager
granular.meaning: Open, number and distribute RFIs you create or manage; set assignees and due dates; close RFIs.

notIncluded: Edit, reopen or delete other users’ RFIs — RFIs Admin.
Configure tool settings or the permissions table — RFIs Admin.

access.levelMeaning: Full control of the project’s RFIs tool: every RFI (edit, reopen, delete), tool configuration, the permissions table and custom reports.

purpose: This procedure defines how [Customer] raises, manages and closes Requests for Information (RFIs) in Procore so design and site queries are answered within the agreed timeframe, every decision is recorded against the project, and cost or programme impacts are identified early. It covers the full RFI lifecycle from draft to closure.

phases.name: Raise
phases.desc: Creator drafts the RFI with one clear question, drawings and photos.

phases.name: Review & send
phases.desc: RFI Manager checks the draft, numbers it and distributes for response.

phases.name: Respond
phases.desc: Assignee answers in Procore; impact on cost and programme is assessed.

phases.name: Close
phases.desc: Official response recorded, registers updated, RFI set to Closed.

procedureIntro: Follow these steps in the Procore RFIs tool. Keep one question per RFI so each response is clear and auditable. Your permission level determines which steps you perform — steps outside your access are handled by the RFI Manager or tool Admin.

steps.title: Prepare the query before opening Procore
steps.body: Confirm the answer is not already available in the current drawing set, specifications or a previous RFI. Gather everything the reviewer needs to answer without a site visit.
bullets: One question per RFI — split multi-part queries into separate RFIs.
Capture site photos and mark up the affected drawing.
Note the drawing number, revision and spec section affected.

callout.label: Why it matters
callout.body: Incomplete RFIs bounce between parties and blow out response times. A well-prepared RFI is usually answered on the first pass.

steps.title: Create the RFI (Draft)
steps.body: Open the project's RFIs tool and select + Create. As a Standard user your RFI is created in Draft status — it is not visible to the design team until the RFI Manager opens and distributes it.
bullets: Subject: [Customer naming convention — e.g. Location – Trade – Query].
Write the question in full, referencing the drawing and spec section.
Complete required fields per project configuration (location, cost/schedule impact if enabled).

callout.label: Cannot do
callout.body: Standard users cannot set the RFI number or Open status — Procore assigns the number when the RFI Manager opens the RFI.

steps.title: Select the RFI Manager and submit
steps.body: Select the RFI Manager from the list (only users with Admin permission or the 'Act as RFI Manager' granular permission appear; the project may enforce a default RFI Manager). Add any Distribution members who should be notified, then save the draft.

callout.label: Handoff
callout.body: Your draft now sits with the RFI Manager. You will be notified when it is opened, and again when the official response is recorded.

steps.title: Review the draft and distribute for response
steps.body: Open the draft RFI assigned to you and act as gatekeeper. Check the question is answerable, then either respond-and-close it directly (if the answer is known) or open it: Procore assigns the RFI number, and you set the Assignee(s) (responsible reviewer) and a Due date within the contract SLA.
bullets: Reject or return unclear drafts to the creator rather than sending poor questions to consultants.
Confirm the assignee is in the project Directory with access to the RFIs tool.
Set the due date per the contract SLA of [X business days].

callout.label: Scope
callout.body: With Standard + 'Act as RFI Manager', you can only manage RFIs you created or where you are the designated RFI Manager.

steps.title: Respond to an RFI you are assigned
steps.body: Open the RFI from the email notification or the RFIs list and record your response directly in Procore — do not reply by email outside the system. Attach any revised drawings or documents. Your response is time-stamped against the project record.
bullets: Answer the question asked; if you cannot, say what is needed and from whom.
Attach superseding documents rather than describing them.

steps.title: Track RFIs relevant to you
steps.body: Use the RFIs list filters (status, assignee, due date, overdue) to monitor items you created or are named on. Visibility of other users' RFIs and closed responses depends on project settings.

callout.label: Note
callout.body: Private RFIs are visible only to their distribution list and tool Admins.

steps.title: Review the response and assess impact
steps.body: When the assignee responds, review the answer for completeness and for cost or programme impact. If the response changes scope, trigger the [Customer] variation / change event process before closing.
bullets: Reassign for input if further review is required.
Flag cost/programme impact to the Commercial Manager per [Customer process].

steps.title: Record the official response and close
steps.body: Mark the accepted answer as the Official Response, confirm the distribution list covers everyone who acts on the answer, then set the RFI to Closed. Ensure superseded drawings are updated in the Drawings tool.

callout.label: Why it matters
callout.body: An unclosed RFI keeps the query legally 'open'. Closing with an official response fixes the decision and its timestamp for the project record.

steps.title: Edit, reopen or delete RFIs (Admin)
steps.body: Admins can edit any RFI, reopen closed items when a response is disputed or superseded, and delete RFIs created in error. Record the reason in the RFI before reopening or deleting so the audit trail stays intact.

callout.label: Control
callout.body: Deleting an RFI should be exceptional — prefer closing with a note. [Customer approval rule for deletions].

steps.title: Configure the RFIs tool (Admin)
steps.body: Set the project's RFI behaviour under Configure Settings: default RFI Manager, RFI number prefix, private RFIs, overdue email reminders, closed-response visibility, and the tool's Permissions Table. Review settings at project start-up and after any process change.
bullets: Align the default due-date/SLA settings with the head contract.
Grant 'Act as RFI Manager' via the permission template, not ad-hoc.

closeoutIntro: Use this checklist before closing any RFI. If something does not behave as described here, work through it in this order: check the common issues table below; confirm your own access in Section 1, since several problems are simply a permission you do not hold; then check the Procore reference guides listed at the foot of this page. If it is still unresolved, contact your Procore Implementation Manager or raise it with Procore Support at support.procore.com, quoting the project name and the RFI number.

checklist.text: One clear question, with drawing/spec references attached
checklist.hint: Multi-part queries split into separate RFIs.

checklist.text: RFI Manager and distribution list set before submitting
checklist.hint: Everyone who acts on the answer is on distribution.
Response answers the question; revised documents attached.

checklist.text: Cost & programme impact assessed before closing
checklist.hint: Variation / change event raised where scope changed.

checklist.text: Response actioned on site / in your deliverables
checklist.hint: Superseded information no longer in use.

checklist.text: Tool settings and permissions table reviewed
checklist.hint: At project start-up and after process changes.

issues.resolution: Confirm they are in the project Directory with RFIs tool access and named as assignee or on distribution; re-add and resend.

issues.issue: Response given by email, not in Procore
issues.resolution: Copy the response into the RFI as the official response (or use the email-in response method if enabled) so the record is complete.
Use the overdue filter; chase per the SLA escalation path [Customer escalation]. Overdue email reminders can be enabled in Configure Settings.

issues.issue: Draft stuck — creator can't send the RFI
issues.resolution: Expected behaviour: Standard users create drafts only. The designated RFI Manager must open and distribute it — check the correct manager is selected.

issues.issue: Wrong number sequence or prefix on RFIs
issues.resolution: Admin reviews the prefix / numbering configuration under Configure Settings; numbering changes affect new RFIs only.
